threat_model.threat_source: AI systems (primary actor); the passage also describes economic processes/systems as contributing to the harms as they become optimized for AI-centric activities: 'the economy,' 'markets,' 'AI-driven economic systems,' and 'economic forces'
threat_model.objective_or_harmful_outcome: No intention or goal is explicitly stated for any actor; the explicitly described harmful outcomes are: AI systems 'might outcompete humans for crucial scarce resources such as land, energy, and raw materials'; 'inflation in these basic resources might make even necessities increasingly unaffordable for humans'; 'economic pressure to reallocate such resources away from human uses'; the economy 'fails to maintain infrastructure and supply chains which are critical for human survival'; 'markets might stop producing resource-intensive human goods'; 'increasing costs of resource-intensive human-centric goods and services' before 'making some necessities effectively unavailable'; 'humans might lose the ability to meaningfully participate in economic decision-making at any level'; it becomes 'impossible for humans to make informed economic decisions or effectively regulate economic activity'; 'humans might become mere subjects of economic forces optimized for purposes beyond their understanding'
threat_model.capability: AI systems 'can utilize these resources more efficiently than humans' (stated conditionally: 'if AI systems can utilize these resources more efficiently than humans'); AI systems 'might outcompete humans for crucial scarce resources such as land, energy, and raw materials'
threat_model.constraints_or_enabling_conditions: 'if AI systems can utilize these resources more efficiently than humans, that will create economic pressure to reallocate such resources away from human uses'; 'If human consumers command an ever-smaller share of economic resources, markets might stop producing resource-intensive human goods in favor of more profitable AI-focused activities'; 'Financial markets might move too quickly for human participants to engage with them' (time pressure on humans); 'the complexity of AI-driven economic systems might exceed human comprehension' (limit on human oversight); 'This could happen gradually and unevenly'
threat_model.target_or_asset_at_risk: Humans ('human consumers,' 'human participants'); humans' access to 'crucial scarce resources such as land, energy, and raw materials' and to 'necessities'; 'infrastructure and supply chains which are critical for human survival'; production of 'resource-intensive human goods' and 'resource-intensive human-centric goods and services'; humans' 'ability to meaningfully participate in economic decision-making at any level'; humans' capacity to 'make informed economic decisions or effectively regulate economic activity'

evidence.threat_source: First, AI systems might outcompete humans for crucial scarce resources such as land, energy, and raw materials. ... the economy might become so optimized for AI-centric activities that it fails to maintain infrastructure and supply chains which are critical for human survival. ... markets might stop producing resource-intensive human goods in favor of more profitable AI-focused activities. ... the complexity of AI-driven economic systems might exceed human comprehension ... humans might become mere subjects of economic forces optimized for purposes beyond their understanding.
